title: Week 11 Analysis
subtitle: Cadegn gains 26 and leads by 28, the biggest lead of the season.
intro_paragraphs: A week ago the top three were separated by one point. Now Cadegn is at 88, the highest total anyone has had this season, and leads Dilger and Dustin (both 60) by 28. The previous biggest lead was 20, also Cadegn's, in Week 4. Cadegn's +26 is the third-biggest week in the pool, behind Dilger's +46 in Week 2 and Cadegn's own +39 in Week 4.

Last week's co-leaders went the other way. Hume lost 9 and fell from 1st to 5th. Mike T lost 12 and fell from 2nd to 6th. Four divisions changed order again: the AFC North, AFC West, NFC North, and NFC South. The Patriots, Seahawks, Rams, Packers, Browns, and Falcons had byes, and two of them (the Browns and Falcons) moved up without playing.

fun_facts.heading: Cadegn Scores in Every Division That Moved
fun_facts.body: Cadegn gained in all four divisions that changed: +9 in the AFC West, +8 in the NFC South, +6 in the NFC North, and +3 in the AFC North. Cadegn now has 6 of 8 division-winner picks currently right (Bengals, Jaguars, Bills, Broncos, Lions, Giants), the most in the pool, and is the only bettor who picked the Giants to win the NFC East. Cadegn also leads every tiebreaker category: 2 perfect divisions, 4 top-2 bonuses, 3 bottom-2 bonuses, and 18 exact hits.

fun_facts.heading: The AFC West Flipped Back
fun_facts.body: Last week we wrote that if the Chiefs and Broncos flipped back, the same 9 points would go the other way for four bettors. They did. Both are 8-2, and Denver is first on a tiebreaker. Cadegn and Dustin (Broncos-Chiefs) each gained 9. Hume and Mike T (Chiefs-Broncos) each lost 9. Dilger and Farmer (Broncos first) gained 3, and Tom (Broncos second) lost 3. The two teams are still tied, so this can happen again next week.

fun_facts.heading: Nobody Picked the Chargers Last
fun_facts.body: The Chargers are 1-9 and last in the AFC West. All seven bettors picked the Raiders last, and the Raiders are third at 4-7. Tom picked the Chargers to win the division. Because no one has the bottom two right, the AFC West has no bottom-2 bonus for anyone, and the best anyone can do there right now is 9.

fun_facts.heading: Bears Over Vikings in the NFC North
fun_facts.body: Detroit and Chicago won and are both 8-2. Minnesota lost and dropped to third at 7-3, and idle Green Bay is still last at 6-4. Dilger, Tom, Cadegn, and Farmer picked Lions-Bears and each gained 6 (the Bears exact plus the top-2 bonus), for 9. Hume was the only bettor with the Vikings second, which was worth 9 last week and is worth 3 now. Mike T and Dustin lost the 3 they had for the Bears in third.

fun_facts.heading: Cadegn's NFC South Bet Pays
fun_facts.body: The Saints lost and dropped to last at 3-7, and the idle Falcons moved up to third, also 3-7. Carolina won and leads at 5-5, Tampa Bay is second at 3-7. Cadegn picked Falcons third and Saints last, so that's two exact plus the bottom-2 bonus: 8 points, up from 0. Dustin, Hume, and Farmer each gained 3. Mike T, Dilger, and Tom lost 3. Nobody picked Carolina first.

fun_facts.heading: The Steelers Are Third, So Everyone Gains 3
fun_facts.body: Pittsburgh lost and fell to 6-4, and the idle Browns (also 6-4) moved ahead of them into second. All seven bettors picked the Steelers third, so all seven gained 3 in the AFC North. Cincinnati lost but is still first at 7-3. Everyone also picked the Browns last, and the Browns are second, with Baltimore (4-7) last instead.

fun_facts.heading: Dilger and Dustin: Tied on Everything
fun_facts.body: Dilger and Dustin are both at 60 and match on every tiebreaker: one perfect division, two top-2 bonuses, two bottom-2 bonuses, and 14 exact hits. It's the third week in a row two bettors are fully tied (Tom and Hume in Week 9, Dilger and Tom in Week 10). Dustin gained 12 and Dilger gained 9, both their best weeks since Week 8. They're tied for 2nd, but 28 points behind 1st.

fun_facts.heading: Mike T and Hume Fall Together
fun_facts.body: Last week we noted Mike T and Hume have identical picks in four divisions, including the AFC West. That's where both lost 9 this week. Combined, they went from 126 points to 105. Tom is 4th at 54, ahead of Hume (also 54) because Tom has two top-2 bonuses to Hume's one. Mike T is 6th at 51.

fun_facts.heading: Farmer's Best Week
fun_facts.body: Farmer gained 15, scoring in all four divisions that moved (+6 NFC North, +3 in the AFC North, AFC West, and NFC South). That's Farmer's best week of the season, one more than the +14 in Week 7. Farmer is 7th at 45 but now 6 behind Mike T, after being 18 behind 6th place a week ago. Farmer has 5 of 8 division-winner picks currently right, second only to Cadegn, and is still the only bettor without a perfect division.

fun_facts.heading: Locks Up to 5
fun_facts.body: With the Steelers in third, 5 of the 8 picks everyone agreed on are holding: the Bills first and Patriots second in the AFC East, the Steelers third in the AFC North, the Lions first in the NFC North, and the Cardinals last in the NFC West. The three broken ones are the Browns last (they're second), the Raiders last (the Chargers are), and the Rams first (the 49ers are 9-1).

closing_paragraph: Cadegn has a 28-point lead and the best tiebreakers, but plenty is still tied: the Broncos and Chiefs at 8-2, the Lions and Bears at 8-2, the Browns and Steelers at 6-4, the Seahawks and Rams at 6-4, and three NFC South teams at 3-7. The Seahawks-Rams tie matters most for the chasers: six bettors have Seattle second and would lose 3 if the Rams passed them, while Cadegn, who has the Seahawks third, would gain 3. Same time next Tuesday.
